The placed black ship squares are: in row 2 column 1 there is a single-square black ship; row 4 column 2 and row 5 column 2 form a vertical two-square black ship. Reasoning: The new ship is a straight 3×1 ship, and it cannot share any boundary point with existing ships, so squares adjacent by side or adjacent by corner to existing ships cannot be used. The single-square ship (2,1) forbids all squares from rows 1 to 3 and columns 1 to 2. The vertical two-square ship (4,2),(5,2) forbids all squares from rows 3 to 5 and columns 1 to 3. The remaining safe squares are: rows 1 and 2 columns 3 to 5, and rows 3, 4, 5 columns 4 to 5. Count consecutive safe positions of length 3: when placed horizontally, row 1 and row 2 each have 1, for a total of 2; when placed vertically, column 4 has 3, column 5 has 3, for a total of 6. Therefore the total number is 2+6=8.

method.method_draft: Use a forbidden-cell map. First read the image as a 5 by 5 grid with existing black ships occupying cells (row 2, column 1) and (rows 4–5, column 2), where rows are counted from top and columns from left. From the text, the new ship is a straight 3 by 1 ship and must not share any boundary point with another ship. Mark every cell forbidden if it is occupied or edge/corner adjacent to an occupied cell. The single cell at (2,1) forbids rows 1–3, columns 1–2; the vertical ship at (4,2),(5,2) forbids rows 3–5, columns 1–3. The remaining safe cells are rows 1–2 columns 3–5, and rows 3–5 columns 4–5. Count length-3 consecutive safe runs: horizontally there are 2, one in each of rows 1 and 2; vertically there are 3 in column 4 and 3 in column 5. Total 2+6=8.
